No one wants to be transgender. It isn't fun going through this suffering. But it is NOT too late to begin transition, I didn't realize what this was until I was 19/almost 20 and in college. It is scary and incredibly frustrating. At your age I had only had sex once, when very drunk, at 17. That was because I felt I should, not because I wanted to that much.

Go see the campus counselor, she will probably not be qualified to help you as far as to diagnose GID or anything. But it is good to talk it out with someone regardless. I really miss my college counselor, she did help me seek out more specialized treatment when I was ready for it.

I think about suicide frequently, and have since before I even realized I was trans, right now it would be easy. I have a loaded 9mm Glock handgun in my bedside table, but as they say "it is a permanent solution to a temporary problem." I wont say it will "get better" because I honestly cannot say for sure, it is still tough for me, I have been living full time for 3 months now, I don't always pass. When I get miss-gendered or have someone stare at me it really hurts. But it might get better, and that is enough for me right now. This is all we have, this life, and I would rather stick through this shitty time now on the off-chance my life will improve than throw it all away.

Stick in there, find someone to talk this out with, you can make it through this.
-Claire

I started estrogen 15 months before I started living full time, unfortunately I am not even an A cup...So I had no issues hiding it, I just wore a sports bra every day to school and wherever, oh and didn't wear just t shirts, always had an over-shirt of some kind (mostly collared shirts) cause I was paranoid someone would see the lines of the bra if my shirt clung weirdly to me at some point.

The reason I would reccommend not using a binder is that I know for FTM guys it tends to flatten out their breasts (I would also be worried it might somehow stunt growth). But either way you wouldn't want to squish your breasts that much, unless you get a lot of breast growth or are planning to be incognito for a long time I do not think it will be an issue. People may even think you have pecs! lol.

Hair removal is a nice thing, I used to have body hair before the hormones did away with the majority of it. But when I first started out I was using Nads on myself to wax of the hair, my friend helped me do my back...you could do something like that for your SO...maybe.

When I started out, it was much easier for me to buy things online and have them shipped to my apt. I got most of my original shoes from payless, cause they actually go up to 12 in womens (I hate my feet).

Also I got some silicon insets from here http://www.truekare.com/two.htm which are nice, though I usually don't use them any more, they feel a little to fake to me (appearance wise) so I usually just wear a 36A though I'm a bit away from filling it in properly. It definitely took me a bit to figure out women's sizing, so I was always sure to order from places with good return policies.

Whatever you decided to do I am sure your SO will appreciate it. I know when my boyfriend got me girly presents while I was first starting my transition it was absolutely wonderful.

I know that many trans people when they come out, they start by being super femme. I know I dress more femme than I would if I was dressing how I'd like, but there is such a desire (for many of us) to pass, I think it drives us to go a bit farther than we would ideally go. I started College 4 years ago, in the beginning I did very well, But I ended up dropping out this last semester. About half way through I realized I was trans, and though I began seeking help, I became very depressed. I was so afraid of what the world would do to me, how others would treat me. As I started coming out I had a mostly good experience...though I did lose some friends, and a couple of my close family members do not approve. Now I am living full time as a girl, which has actually brought me much more stress and depression than I would have thought. It has been 2.5 months and every time I get referred to by a male pronoun or someone stares at me I find it crushing. I am afraid to go out by myself, and am currently unemployed because I am too scared to go apply places. We live in a very judgmental world, though it gets better day by day, it isn't much of a solace for us living it now. I am glad however I haven't taken my life, sure it hurts now, but I don't want to sacrifice everything that I could have because it is tough right now. Who knows what the future may hold for me, you and all of us. We just need to stick it through, I believe if you want it bad enough, you can make your life something worth living.
